newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end virtually flat in record volume.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end virtually flat in record volume.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended virtually flat amid soaring volume Thursday, as domestic equity funds continued to pour money into the market.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most traded stocks closed off 0.01 percent at 12,205 points.
Market turnover totalled 1.47 billion reais ($1.36 billion), the highest volume since September 15, 1994, excluding options settlement dates.
The bolsa opened higher, still reacting to Wednesday's lower house approval of the General Telecommunications Law, but lost strength late in the session on some profit-taking.
Power stocks suffered most from the profit-taking wave, which helped weaken the index. percent to close at 615.01 reais, while Minas Gerais state power utility Cemig lost 0.73 percent to 54.60 reais.
Sao Paulo state power firm Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) fell 2.36 percent to 165 reais.
While investors took profits on electrical stocks, telecommunications stocks, particularly Telebras, and some second-tier shares kept trading higher.
Telebras preferred gained 0.45 percent to 157.20 reais. But the highest rise was seen by Telebras voting stock, which rose 1.77 percent to 142.99 reais.
Telebras continued to account for most of the trade, brokers said.
Daily average trade has been steadily rising in recent weeks as local investors have been moving from fixed-income funds into equity funds, analysts said.
"It is pretty much domestic players who have been behind the bolsa's rally," said a senior trader at a local investment bank. "Foreign participation has not increased much."
In fact, the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) registered in the first 10 days of June net foreign capital outflows of 84.9 million reais.
According to the latest statistics, foreign buys in the period totalled 1.648 billion reais, while foreign sales amounted to 1.733 billion reais.
